clue.text: Reaction as a skirt bottom's shown behind?

indicators.note: behind places the skirt bottom after the single letter in the answer

parts.note: the bottom edge of a skirt is its hem

explanation.surface: Someone clears their throat on noticing a glimpse of the back of a skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate little cough is a reaction used to draw attention or show disapproval.

clue.text: From part of Europe, one to be found in an atlas, perhaps

indicators.note: to be found in says the one letter sits inside the other piece
perhaps hints that the letters of an atlas are only a possible arrangement, so they are reshuffled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Looking for a European region by scanning an atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AN ATLAS into ALSATAN, and 'to be found in' puts I (one) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace is a region of France, and its people and things are Alsatian.

clue.text: Woman covering head, eager to conceal lines

indicators.note: to conceal means one piece wraps round and hides the other
covering the head hides the first letter, so the word for eager loses its opening

parts.note: someone eager is keen

explanation.surface: A keen woman with her head covered hides some lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering head' hides the first letter of the word for eager, and 'to conceal' wraps what remains round the lines; 'Woman' is just any female name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a female first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Lesbian, possibly, one facing calumny

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
calumny is a false damaging statement, a slander

explanation.surface: A gay woman confronting malicious gossip about herself.
explanation.walkthrough: Lesbian here means a native of Lesbos, a Greek island, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Lesbos, a Greek island, lives on an island, so is an example of an island dweller.

clue.text: Bit of leg found on archaeological exercise causes disturbance

parts.note: the shin is the front part of the lower leg
an archaeological excavation is a dig

explanation.surface: A leg bone unearthed at an excavation stirs up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a noisy party or a commotion, a rowdy disturbance.

clue.text: Alpine sun clear? Rather obscured in this

definitions.text: Alpine sun clear? Rather obscured in this

indicators.note: obscured means the letters of the phrase before it are blurred into a new order

explanation.surface: Is the mountain sun bright? No, it is partly blocked out in this event.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: in this event the sun is far from clear, being partly covered, while 'obscured' also scrambles ALPINE SUN CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: In this kind of solar event the moon covers the centre of the sun, leaving a bright ring, so the sun is partly hidden.

clue.text: Detached crumpled notice, leading to discovery of culprit

parts.note: det. is the abbreviation for detached, as in house adverts

indicators.note: crumpled means the word notice is crushed into a different order

explanation.surface: A notice was torn down and screwed up, which led to the culprit being found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' turns NOTICE into ECTION; DET is the estate-agent abbreviation for a detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: Detection is the act of finding out who committed a crime.

clue.text: In car I decided to take a journey

indicators.note: In tells us the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Sitting in the car, I made up my mind to set off on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel, as on a horse or in a vehicle.

clue.text: Erect revolting structures? One gives an explanation

indicators.note: structures, used as a verb, means building the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Ugly buildings being put up, with someone offering a justification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erect' and 'revolting' look like the surface's verb and adjective, but they are the letters to be rearranged; 'structures' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A covering letter accompanies an application or document, explaining what is enclosed and why.

clue.text: Measure that is suitable for hunter's assistant

parts.note: a gill is a small measure of liquid, a quarter pint

explanation.surface: A suitable measure for a hunter's helper.
explanation.walkthrough: A gillie is a Scottish attendant on a hunting or fishing trip; 'suitable for' simply links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a ghillie guides and helps a sportsman when shooting deer or fishing.

clue.text: Hopelessly inept Dean endlessly foolish, impossible to reason with

indicators.note: hopelessly signals that the letters which follow are thrown into disorder
endlessly means the word foolish loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A dean who is clumsy and silly will not listen to argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts FOOLISH to FOOLIS; 'Hopelessly' rearranges that with INEPT DEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-opinionated is so sure of their own views that argument will not move them.

clue.text: Went underground to inform editor about subversive nun

indicators.note: about means the word for inform goes round the other piece

parts.note: to inform someone is to tell them

indicators.note: subversive suggests overturning, so the letters of nun are upset

explanation.surface: A convent informer reports to a newspaper editor about a rebellious nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subversive' scrambles the nun, and 'about' puts the word for inform round that scramble, with the editor tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To tunnel is to dig a passage below ground, so tunnelled is to have moved beneath the surface.

clue.text: Tie up Latin expert

parts.note: an ace is someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: A classics scholar is asked to bind something.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace something, such as shoes, is to fasten it with cords.

clue.text: Team I'll upset, beating every former effort

indicators.note: upset means the letters of these words are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: I'll beat the team by a record margin.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record surpasses every previous performance.

clue.text: Help, offer use of a worker

parts.note: to lend is to let someone use something for a time
a hand is a manual labourer, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Offering the services of a labourer as assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in and assist someone is to give practical aid.

clue.text: Good story about Irish not suitable for lads

parts.note: a story can mean a falsehood, a lie

explanation.surface: A good Irish tale that the boys would not enjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Girlie things are aimed at or typical of girls, so boys would steer clear.

clue.text: Not all rest easily in this county

parts.note: some means a part rather than the whole

indicators.note: easily suggests the word rest is loosely rearranged

explanation.surface: Not everybody can relax comfortably in this part of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'easily' turns REST into RSET. SOMERSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English shire in the south-west, an example of a county.

clue.text: Horseman who could be taken on board

definitions.meaning: a mounted warrior of medieval times

definitions.text: who could be taken on board
definitions.meaning: a chess piece shaped like a horse's head, which can be captured on the chessboard

explanation.definitionFit: A medieval mounted soldier holds that title, and the chess piece of the same name can be captured during a game.

clue.text: Restaurant in which army entertains navy after a victory

indicators.note: entertains means the army word plays host, holding the rest inside

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

indicators.note: after places the navy abbreviation behind the victory letters

parts.note: VE is victory in Europe, as in VE Day
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: In this eatery the army hosts the navy to celebrate a win.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is Britain's Territorial Army and VE stands for Victory in Europe (VE Day, 1945).
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek eating house.

clue.text: On back to preserve party? impossible!

indicators.note: back means the little word on is read the other way

parts.note: to preserve food is to can it
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Asked to save the party, someone refuses outright.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal phrase is a flat refusal meaning that something cannot be done.

clue.text: New clue I changed: "centres"

indicators.note: changed means the letters of clue I are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A setter announces a new revised clue whose answer is centres.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclei are cores or central points, the plural of nucleus.

clue.text: Fish catch a Kerryman nets

indicators.note: nets means the phrase holds the letters within it, as a net holds a catch

explanation.surface: A man from County Kerry lands a fish in his nets.
explanation.walkthrough: A Kerryman is a man from County Kerry in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hake is a sea fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Being active can somehow protect against disease

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of active can are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: Being energetic may in some way keep illness away.
explanation.definitionFit: To vaccinate is to inoculate someone so they gain immunity.

clue.text: One's right to order a distinctive fragrance

parts.note: one is A, as in a single item
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone is entitled to order a particular scent.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell, a characteristic scent.

clue.text: Water seen in sea quakes

indicators.note: seen in says the letters can be spotted within the following words

explanation.surface: Water witnessed during an earthquake at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqua is the Latin word for water, used in English as well.

clue.text: Old trials resulting in shorter terms?

definitions.meaning: former English courts held four times a year, abolished in 1971
read literally, sittings that last only a quarter, so briefer periods

explanation.walkthrough: These were English county courts held four times a year until 1971; the second reading takes the name literally as quarter-length sessions.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic courts sat once in each three-month period of the year, and a quarter-length session is a shorter term.

clue.text: New party in Scottish island, representing mountainous region?

indicators.note: in places the new party inside the island

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A new political party on a Scottish island claims to speak for the highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Arran is an island off south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An Andorran comes from Andorra, a small country high in the Pyrenees mountains.

clue.text: Lure of cricketer taking one in

indicators.note: taking means the cricketer word takes the other piece inside

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A cricket player is tempted by taking someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is something used to entice, as food on a hook.
